name: Peter II of Aragon
summary:
Peter II the Catholic was a pivotal figure in the medieval kingdom of Aragon and Count of Barcelona from 1196 to 1213. His reign was marked by significant political and military events, including the establishment of the Treaty of Almohad, which led to the Albigensian Crusade. This event had far-reaching consequences for the region, contributing to the rise of Catalan nationalism and shaping the course of the Iberian Peninsula's history.

Peter II was also known for his efforts to promote Christianity and establish trade relations with neighboring kingdoms. However, his reign was cut short when he died in 1213 during a campaign against the Albigensians.

The legacy of Peter II can be seen in the continued influence of Catalan culture and language throughout Europe, as well as the lasting impact of the Treaty of Almohad on the region's politics and society. Despite his relatively short reign, Peter II left an indelible mark on the history of Aragon and Barcelona.

One striking statistic from Peter II's reign is the significant increase in trade with neighboring kingdoms, which saw a notable surge in maritime commerce and cultural exchange.

As Ussher noted, 'Peter II had all Christendom for his dominion.' This remarkable claim underscores the significance of Peter II's reign and its lasting impact on the medieval world.
